text: But let us not forget that families do not exist in a vacuum.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They depend on a supportive ecosystem of opportunities, resources and workplaces that enable them to flourish.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As a member of the business community, I speak not only to lend my support to this Motion, but also to shed light on the vital role businesses, particularly small and medium enterprises (SMEs), play in shaping a family-friendly Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: But beyond their economic contributions, SMEs bring something deeply personal to their role, a genuine understanding of family priorities.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Many SME owners are not just business leaders.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They are also fathers, mothers, husbands and wives who intimately understand the challenges of balancing work and family.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They have experienced the struggle of managing a growing family while meeting the relentless demands of running a business.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: For our business owners, their employees are often more than just workers.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, not uncommon for these business owners to quietly offer financial help to an employee facing unexpected challenges, a gesture rooted in a deep desire to support.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Some celebrate the birth of an employee's child by giving extra cash "hongbao", while others invest in their employees' families by sponsoring bursaries and scholarships, or funding school supplies for their children.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In times of family emergencies, many SME owners go further, extending not only financial assistance, but also additional time-off to help employees focus on what truly matters.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: These acts of care and support are often invisible.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They are not captured by Government surveys or reflected in national statistics and their true impact on families and communities often goes under-reported.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, they demonstrate that being pro-business does not go against the grain of being pro-worker.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, SME owners and their employees are partners in a shared commitment to success, one built on trust, mutual support and a deep understanding that businesses thrive when their people do, reinforcing the idea that economic success and employee well-being are not mutually exclusive, but intertwined.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, while we celebrate and recognise the kindness and generosity of our SMEs, we must also acknowledge the very real operational challenge they face.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Many SMEs operate under tight margins, grappling with manpower shortages, rising cost and the need to stay competitive.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: While larger corporations may have the resources to implement FWAs or extended parental leave, smaller enterprises struggle with the cost of hiring temporary replacement or redistributing workload.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that even as we strive to do more for Singaporeans and build stronger family support systems, we must consider the realities of SMEs.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By addressing these challenges with practical and targeted solutions, we can enable them to remain viable while continuing to play their vital role in supporting families and communities.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: I spoke previously about the operational strain SMEs face when employees take extended leave, especially during peak seasons like Chinese New Year that just happened, for those in retail business or in highly specialised roles, like in the security sector or project management within the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, for smaller businesses with lean teams, the absence of even one key employee can have a significant impact on daily operations.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Even as we prepare for the increase of Government-Paid Paternity Leave and Shared Parental Leave, both laudable initiatives, these challenges are amplified.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Re-integrating employees after extended leave also requires careful planning to maintain productivity.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This additional support could help offset the operational impact of SMEs during this critical transition period.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: To address broader challenges, I had also previously proposed that trade associations and chambers (TACs) work with the Government to establish shared pools of talent that SMEs can tap into during periods of employee absence.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: These shared resources can provide temporary staffing for parental leave coverage, ensuring that businesses can maintain operations without overburdening existing staff.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This can be particularly helpful for specialised roles or roles requiring certification, where finding suitable replacement on short notice is often a challenge.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: I continue to be hopeful that the Government will work with TACs in this regard.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As such, beyond policies and operational fixes, it is crucial to foster an environment where employees feel valued and supported.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: From my earlier speech on mental health, I emphasised the importance of work-life harmony strategies that balance operational needs with employee well-being.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: FWAs, like those found in the new tripartite guidelines on FWAs requests are one way to achieve this balance, but the true culture of care goes further.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It requires intentional efforts from leaders and human resource (HR) teams to create an environment of respect, inclusion and support.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: However, achieving this vision requires a focused effort on HR management.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: SMEs, in particular, may struggle with limited HR resource or expertise.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, my next recommendation is for the Government to continue supporting companies in upskilling HR professionals and senior managers.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This could involve working closely with organisations, such as the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) and then Singapore Human Resources Institute (SHRI), to build these critical competencies.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Businesses that adopt family-friendly practices should be acknowledged for their efforts.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: We should start a public awareness campaign publicising best practices and success stories to inspire others, highlighting companies that have successfully implemented family-friendly policies, especially SMEs that have overcome resource constraints to do so, can demonstrate that such initiatives are not only achievable but also beneficial to both employees and businesses alike.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In many of my previous speeches, I have underscored the importance of integrating a recognition framework with tangible economic incentives to drive meaningful change.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By linking recognitions with practical incentives, we can amplify the ripple effect of progressive practices across industries.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This approach not only rewards companies for doing their part but also ensures they remain competitive in a challenging economic environment.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: But even as we strive towards this vision, we must also keep an eye on the bigger picture.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore competes on a global scale where multinational enterprises have choices.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They choose Singapore because of our skilled workforce, reliable infrastructure and stable policies.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: These are advantages we have cultivated over decades and they have made us a hub of innovation, commerce and opportunity.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This underscores the delicate balance we must maintain.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: We, therefore, cannot afford to take this position for granted.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As regional economies develop, offering younger, increasingly educated and more cost-effective labour forces, they present compelling alternatives for global businesses.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This is a sobering reality, but it is also a call to action, to remain relevant and competitive.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: We must ensure that our policy strikes the right balance, one that supports family, while preserving the economic vibrancy that makes Singapore a place where businesses want to operate and people want to live.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Family-friendly policies, need to be pragmatic, empathetic and offers solutions that benefit and support everyone in the family ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These include working parents, single parents, grandparents, caregivers and employers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement and NTUC's Women's Committee have long championed a Singapore that supports families, advocating for workplace policies that balance career and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Navigating the workplace successfully, charting out happy plans for family and reaching for our own personal North Stars are age-old perennial Singaporean aspirations, and is something that that the NTUC and this House has worked hard to enable and equip Singaporeans to achieve.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we have made significant strides, including stronger workplace fairness laws, improved FWAs, enhanced caregiver support, there is still much work to be done.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we will release the full survey results nearer our International Women's Day celebrations, these early findings highlight the collective voices of our workers and the continued need to carry on our advocacy to ease financial burdens, improve work-life balance and, of course, provide accessible support systems to foster family growth.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement has been advocating for FWAs since the 1990s and caregivers have shared that FWAs are their most preferred form of support in balancing work and caregiving.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: These guidelines are designed to address the fact that every caregiver's needs are unique and that these needs may evolve depending on job requirements and business realities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the Co-Chair to the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements Tripartite Workgroup, the NTUC not only played an instrumental role in drafting the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements but also collaborated with industry partners and employers to publish briefing papers on FWAs, offering actionable insights to help employers implement these arrangements effectively and more importantly, sustainably.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: FWAs must be sustainable and create win-win outcomes for both employers and employees alike.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We call on our employers to continue their implementation of progressive and fair FWA practices in line with the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Such practices would include setting up clear outcomes-based key performance indicators for our employees, implementing more frequent and regular check-ins with staff, and upskilling/equipping HR personnel with current FWA practices.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We too call on the Government to provide more resources to progressive employers, especially lesser resourced SMEs, on implementing programmes and policies.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: FWAs and Workplace Fairness Practices forms just a part of a broader caregiving ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Other initiatives, such as parental leave and caregiving support, such as childcare services, trusted helpers at home, completes this ecosystem of comprehensive support for women and their families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: A union sister summed up the sentiments of the working mom best: "It is not that women do not want to return to work after having a child.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many women can, in fact, strike a good balance between family and work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, what women need most is peace of mind when they are back in the workplace and the very thing that will cause a woman to give up her career is the absence of a trusted network of care for her children".

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The NTUC is no stranger to this sentiment, and a needle-moving move that the NTUC made in the 1970s was to create an island-wide network of childcare centres to provide that exact peace of mind to mothers when they return to work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This network of childcare centres would be later known as MyFirstSkool and today, MyFirstSkool continues to provide affordable childcare, supporting mothers returning to the workforce.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Many mothers also rely on their domestic helpers to provide trusted support at home to care for their children while they are out at work.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The NTUC Women Committee noted that first time employers of migrant domestic workers (MDWs) often need help in navigating the complexities of employer-helper relations.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To support our mothers, we launched a new initiative in 2024 and it is called "To-Gather: Power of Women".

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This initiative brings together resources and partners, such as the Association of Employment Agencies and the NTUC's Centre for Domestic Employees, to strengthen relationships between caregivers and their MDWs via fun care-carnivals and awards recognising good relations between MDWs and their employers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Feedback from our mothers, and fathers of course, is that this initiative has proven to be effective in fostering trust and understanding, and we call on the Government to provide more resources to employers of MDWs in this respect.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In 2012, the Labour Movement called on the Government to introduce two weeks of paid paternity leave and today, we see that evolve into four weeks.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This new Shared Parental Leave scheme offers parents the flexibility to decide how to share their parental leave, something the Labour Movement has long championed.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This flexibility ensures that parents can make the best decisions for their families and we thank the Government for heeding our workers' call for shared parental leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we have made significant strides, there is still much more to be done.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: SME employers with less resourcing often struggle to find temporary replacements when their staff go on parental leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This burden frequently falls on other colleagues and this can be overwhelming, especially in smaller teams.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: SME owners may also face financial strain when reimbursing employees for parental leave.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In modern-day Singapore, Mr Deputy Speaker, the lack of workplace support or facilities should never be a factor for a mother who chooses to breastfeed.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While majority of employers we speak with have provisioned for adequate lactation spaces, we still hear from the ground, women who have to use toilet cubicles to express their breastmilk or to store their expressed milk in communal fridges, next to someone's salad or packed lunch.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is with this, that the NTUC Women and Family Unit implemented the Better Workplace Programme to support progressive family-friendly employers with lactation and wellness spaces for employees.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This programme comes as an extension of our 2013 Project Gold initiative that helped to raise awareness of the needs of breastfeeding mothers in the workplace.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our survey respondents also spoke about the financial pressures they face while raising a family and have indicated that they hope for more financial assistance and subsidies for families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I believe that this would need to be taken with the view of providing more employment opportunities for return-to-work mothers, or mothers entering the workforce for the first time.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would allow for sustainable long-term financial independence instead of dependency on Government subsidies alone.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Joanne joined the "C U Back at Work" Programme in February 2024 after being a stay-at-home mother for over a decade.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With caregiving responsibilities for her three kids, she found it difficult to re-enter the workforce, especially due to her lack of technical skills.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: After being referred to the programme through MSF, she appreciated the supportive, pressure-free learning environment and the flexibility to choose her working location.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Now, she oversees housekeeping matters for, not one but two banks and she remains positive about learning and believes that more women could benefit from FWAs and an empathetic employer.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The combination of FWAs, paired with fair wages and good career pathways is a winning combo to help women get back into the workforce in a smooth, dignified fashion.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Recently, I have in my MPS met with several expectant mothers who have fallen on tough times.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Ms R, not her real name, has two children and is now expecting her third child.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: She has a troubled marriage and after being thrown out of her home by her soon-to-be ex-husband, she needs to find work to support her family.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: She is finding the job hunt process hard, as many employers, fair or otherwise, are concerned about her pregnancy status and ability to continue with work once she delivers.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Labour Movement remains steadfast in our commitment to support working families in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We will continue to advocate for family-friendly workplaces, greater flexibility for caregivers and stronger support for all parents as they balance their work and family responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With the support of the tripartite partnership, I am confident that we can build a future where Singapore families continue to thrive.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: I appreciate the initiative by hon Members Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Ms Hany Soh in tabling this Motion.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: It is of utmost importance that we continue to review and regularly update our policies to better support families, marriage and the parenthood aspirations of Singaporeans wholeheartedly.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: The family is a fundamental unit of society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Where the family is functioning well, it is an anchor point from which we begin our lives, a home base from which we start exploring the world beyond and in times of need and crisis, a place of safety where most of us return to.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: The family is a source of motivation and strength, a place where we first learn to form our social bonds and shape our identity.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: The family is where values, behaviours and character are shaped; where discipline, resilience and morality are nurtured; and where traditions, cultures and heritage are preserved.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: A stable family unit contributes directly to a functional and flourishing society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: If we fail at the first unitary building block of society, it will be incredibly challenging, in fact, impossible, for us to do well as a society and as a nation.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: We all hope for families to remain intact at the outset, that their children eventually do well in school, mature emotionally and socially, and grow into good persons of character and fulfil their parental aspirations.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: We also hope that familial relationships remain firmly intact throughout their lives.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: However, Mr Deputy Speaker, the truth is families can fail, marriages can be upended and parenthood aspirations can go awry, the effects of which can be damaging for both partners and their children.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: The inter-generationality of the impact in broken families is clear and we need to be resolute to break the cycle, difficult as it may be.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Of course, the starting point should always be to reinforce systemic support for an intact family and buttress families for success.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: However, it should not be that in the case where families break down in the first instance, that we have fewer levers to recalibrate our efforts to help these families.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: We should spare no effort for the single parents, their children and their extended family to get back on their feet, to come together as any other family would and to be supported as part of our society.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: I refer to blended families as those that comprise a couple, any children that they have together, as well as any children from their previous relationships as part of the current family unit.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Single-parent families could occur in cases of marital separation and discord, as well as through grief and loss of a partner.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: It can be challenging and lonely for a single parent to manage the multiplicity of challenges, which may bear on his or her shoulders alone.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: If there is grief over the passing of partner, young children in tow, coupled with the need to continue working and feed the family in spite of a turbulent emotional state of affairs, this becomes even more complex and challenging to handle.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Blended families are also unique in their own way.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: However, what blended families suggest is that, perhaps, despite initial challenges or difficulties from the first marriage, both parents show a willingness to look past a painful period in their lives, still with every hope and desire to nurture another relationship forward.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: It suggests that the institution of family remains a key part of their lives despite what may have happened.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: While we structure most of our policy towards raising and strengthening a family unit in the traditional sense, we should recognise there would be very unique challenges in single-parent or blended settings that need support and should be helped with the same, if not more, rigour.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Children remain the most vulnerable in these families and it is something that we must pay attention to.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Where there is a gap in fulfilling the policy intent to support such families, which are distinct and different in the traditional sense, we must be flexible enough to accommodate up to the last mile for them, especially in their time of need.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: My second hope is that the Government also strengthens familial support structures beyond the initial nuclear family.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: From a policy perspective, it would always be easier to calibrate support at the unitary level of a family; the father, the mother and their children.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: The age-old saying goes, Mr Deputy Speaker: "it takes a village to raise a child".

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: I do hope these are areas that the Government will look into as we work towards strengthening our families, our marriages and our journeys in parenthood.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
text: Ultimately, it is with a hope that Singapore remains safe and conducive for our children and their own families to grow and benefit in turn.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: It is a topic I have spoken on many times in Parliament since I first became a father 10 years ago and I experienced many of the joys as well as challenges that young couples in Singapore face.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Over this time, I have also witnessed the significant strides that the Government has made to support families at every stage of life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Tripartite partners have also drawn up the guidelines on FWA requests to support employers in offering FWAs more tailored to individual needs, including those of young parents, as shared by fellow labour Member, Ms Yeo Wan Ling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: To support young parents in returning to work, the Government has increased and will double the availability of infant care places in the next five years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: The Government has also improved access to affordable homes for families, through the First-Timer (Parents and Married Couples) priority category and the one-year Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (Open Market) Voucher.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: These are substantial support appreciated by our unionists and young parents.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Our collective efforts are building a stronger foundation for families to grow and thrive in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: However, some young couples still struggle to juggle their parenthood aspirations with other career aspirations and caregiving priorities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: I want to highlight three key areas where we can better support them in managing these trade-offs in their marriage and parenthood journey.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Many young couples today are supporting their parents at the same time as caring for children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: For those who wish to have three or more children, I note that the Government already provides additional support to help manage costs, such as a larger Baby Bonus Cash Gift, higher co-matching for the CDA and higher parenthood tax rebates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: However, these families still need help to manage daily costs and it applies to those with more than one child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Time is too, and perhaps even more so.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: During my house visit over the weekend, a young mother of two children lamented that childcare leave is her greatest need.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: She is a social worker, which is a highly intensive vocation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: To her, the current childcare leave allocation works well for parents with only one child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: As all parents know, we all know full well that children do not fall ill at the same time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: They conspire sometimes to always fall sick consecutively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: The cycles of flu then require multiple trips to the doctor’s and home rest, and the cycles then repeat themselves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: I encourage efforts to see how we can further support these families, for example, through increased childcare leave for families with more than one child.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: We would also need to regularly review the costs faced by young couples in child-raising, especially on childcare necessities and provide more childcare support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Next, on more options for couples to start a family later.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Some women do prefer to start a family later, when they are more established in their careers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: For women, sometimes their best years for bearing children would also be the years when they are advancing their careers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: They aspire to have children and want the flexibility to have children later in life when they are also more established in their careers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Studies suggest that egg freezing and thawing at a younger age provides a higher pregnancy success rate than using fresh eggs or embryos for women starting families later during assisted reproductive technology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: To support women in their reproductive choices, 11% of companies with more than 500 employees and 19% of companies with more than 20,000 employees in the US included egg freezing in the coverage of their fertility benefits in 2020.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: As the benefits of egg freezing become more widely recognised, I hope Singapore employers can lean forward to offer fertility benefits, including egg freezing, to support their female staff who would like the flexibility of having children later in life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: In addition, subsidies are available for ART treatments like IVF, but these are accessible to women below the age of 40 and are limited to procedures conducted in public hospitals.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Given the rising age of first-time mothers and the advances in medical technology, I would like to reiterate my call from 2017 to adopt a more nuanced approach, rather than removing subsidies entirely for women above 40, subsidies could be progressively reduced or adjusted according to a health assessment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: And such subsidies can be offered in the private sector too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: We need to give more support to our mothers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Many of them make sacrifices in their careers to care for their families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Research over the last 20 years shows that there remains a wage gap between men and women, and this is due mainly to the impact on their wages when women interrupt their careers to have children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Interestingly, according to a 2023 Pew Research Centre study, while having children often leads to less pay for mothers, fatherhood leads to an increase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Men with children typically earn more than both women with or without kids and men without children.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: I must admit that this is an overseas study, but perhaps, worthwhile for us to study this further too.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Therefore, I encourage companies that can and should step up and do more to close the gender pay gap.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Last year, I encourage HR practitioners to reconsider some of the common performance evaluation criteria in practice today.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: For example, should the performance of women on maternity leave be assessed based on the full year, or just based on the eight months, during which they were at work?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Companies can also take a longer-term view to create more options for women.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: When mothers are ready to come back, companies can offer "returnship" programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: These combine upskilling, on-the-job training and mentorship that help mothers reintegrate into the workplace.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Globally, major companies like Goldman Sachs, Amazon and Chevron already offer such programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: I hope to see more employers follow their example, so that we can play our part in helping mothers resume their careers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: We should support young couples with aspirations for larger families.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: We should enable more options for women to conceive later in life and we should give more recognition to women who make career sacrifices to care for family.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines):
text: Let us help our young Singaporeans to be the parents they aspire to be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Motion calls for the continued review and updating of policies to better support families, as well as the marriage and parenthood aspirations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It also calls for a whole-of-society approach to build a "Singapore Made for Families".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Families are not merely biological, social or legal connections, they are the cornerstone of our communities and the source of love, security and guidance necessary to shape individuals, the community and ultimately, our nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Families are our first educators, our caregivers, our protectors and our emotional anchors; and the concept of family resonates deeply with the many cultural traditions present in Singapore, where marriage and parenthood are welcomed and celebrated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This is particularly relevant in the context of today's Motion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Families are our past, present and future, and need to be cherished.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We must ensure that our families are strong, healthy and resilient, and that everyone within a family unit is supported and empowered to stand together as a single, unified entity. : Mr Deputy Speaker, I will now touch on some of the contemporary challenges faced by parents and families in Singapore and then suggest some initiatives to assist and support parents and families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Before highlighting these challenges, I would like to note that Singapore has a commendable track record when it comes to supporting parents and families and has already implemented a suite of innovative and successful policies and programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is clear that families are a priority across the Singapore Government, community and private sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our commitment to making Singapore a nation that supports families is ongoing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, laws and policies alone cannot change personal attitudes and behaviours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The challenges I will address today are reflections of our reality and in reviewing how we best support families, it is important to engage all stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Creating a family-friendly Singapore is a collective effort, involving not just the Government, but everyone in our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: An article published by TODAY, on 13 August 2024, loan applications from middle-age Singaporeans have surged due to rising living costs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: This suggests that the middle class may be at greater risk of unsustainable debt cycles driven by escalating household expenses, medical cost and credit card debts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And the TODAY Youth Survey in 2022, reported that 52% of young people consider the cost of living as a major source of mental health struggles.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In a 2022 study by Randstad, 70% of Singaporeans reported having a poor work-life balance, primarily due to overwhelming workloads.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In 2023, a survey by the ADP Research Institute found that 40% of Singaporean employees think they work up to 10 unpaid hours weekly and that this time often includes working during lunch breaks and staying late.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Notably, over 50% of parents with newborns in Singapore feel they put in up to 10 extra unpaid hours each week.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And in 2023, a survey by Randstad found that 41% of employees in Singapore were considering leaving their current jobs in search of better work-life balance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's education system is internationally recognised for its rigorous academic standards, attention given to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education and effective bilingual policy and consistently produces high-achieving students in international assessments like Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA).

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore would not be the global success story it is today without our schools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, emphasis on academic performance and accompanying pressure to perform well in exams and standardised testing, has been linked to increasing mental health issues among students, including stress, burnout, anxiety and depression.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: A 2017 report by the OECD showed that 86% of Singaporean students were worried about poor grades at school, compared to the OECD average of 66% and 76% of Singaporean students reported feeling very anxious for a test even if they were well-prepared, compared to the OECD average of 55%.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Another issue impacting on families is that of the increasing use of "social media".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Through social media, everyone, including very young children, is increasingly exposed to illicit, disturbing, meaningless or untrue information and there has been an accompanying rise in mental health issues, developmental disorders and learning disabilities among children and young people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For example, a 2016 study by DQ Institute and the Nanyang Technological University showed that 77% of 12-year-olds in Singapore are active on social media and chat apps, and spend an average of six and a half hours on these daily; and that 55% of nine-year-olds actively use social media and chat apps, and spend an average of three and a half hours on these daily.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The same study showed that even moderate amount of time spent on digital screens can lead to disturbed sleep, memory lapses, weight gain, spine and neck problems, poor school performance, depression and poorly developed social and communication skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: A 2023 study by Institute of Mental Health reported that excessive social media use is one of three factors linked to mental health symptoms among young people, including symptoms of depression, anxiety and stress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Phubbing is a combination of the words "phone" and "snubbing", refers to the act of ignoring your immediate social interactions, in favour of engaging with a smartphone.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Phubbing is increasingly common with adults, children and young people, all choosing to interact with a digital device than another person.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Phubbing within families can have a significant impact on the health and well-being of the individuals within the family and the family as a unit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For example, a 2023 research publication from China looked at the relationship between parental phubbing and mobile phone addiction in junior high school students, showed that parental phubbing significantly disrupt the parent-child relationship, which in turn led to higher levels of mobile phone addiction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: And a 2024 publication on systemic review and meta analysis on the relationship between parental phubbing and adolescence depressive symptoms, showed that parental phubbing poses a significant threat to children's social-emotional development, disrupts parent-child interactions and contributes to feelings of neglect and reduced emotional connection for children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Men and women want different things today than they did before and this has had a significant impact on how, when and why families are formed, how they live and whether they have children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: For example, traditional multi-generational households are becoming less common as young adults prioritise independence, career, delayed marriage and smaller family units.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Dual-income households are more common, with a greater emphasis on shared parenting and work-life balance, and non-traditional family structures, including single-parent and blended families, are gaining recognition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Reasons given for not having children included, the rising cost of living, pressures of a demanding education system, insufficient time to spend with their children and a lack of confidence in their parenting knowledge and skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Before I do so, I should note that successful implementation of these initiatives will require cooperative partnerships between the Government, community and private sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We cannot simply fall back on the assumption that this is all the Government's responsibility and we all have a role to play in supporting families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Third, establish a family ambassadors programme to train and empower family ambassadors within communities to provide advice, guidance, support and resources to families in need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, create family innovation hubs that provide safe, age and culturally appropriate spaces where families can share issues and co-create with other parents, or families, innovative solutions to their challenges, such as collaborative childcare models or shared community resources.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Fifth, establish Human Libraries, where people act as "living books" and share their real-life experiences and personal stories with "readers" through one-to-one or small group conversations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Sixth, developing a family well-being index that measures family well-being and that can guide policy decisions and highlight areas of service delivery needing improvement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Seventh, provide free universal marriage preparation courses to assist newlyweds, engaged couples and those contemplating marriage, to develop the skills, knowledge and mindset for a strong and lasting marriage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Eighth, continue the work already been done to address gender inequality, particularly through programmes that assist to challenge and shift the traditional gender norms that are attributed to women and men.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Ninth, encourage agencies to review and update existing policies and programmes to ensure that they recognise and are relevant to the diverse range of families, including single-parent and blended families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Tenth, monitor international developments regarding access to social media and the use of digital devices, particularly by children and young people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Alternatively, be innovative and lead the world in addressing what is an emerging public health crisis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Eleventh, undertake a review of the Singapore education system, including consideration of whether reliance on exams and standardised testing is in the best interests of children, young people and their families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Despite the importance and value of marriage and parenthood, shifting social and economic factors in Singapore, some of which I discussed above, mean that the concept and practice of "family" is changing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As I have indicated in my speech, families play a special role in Singapore and are a critical element in the continuity of our culture, society and nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We must continue to cherish and nourish families and do so in a way that recognises the ever-changing nature of what it is to be a family and the challenges that families face.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that by working together, hand in hand, we can achieve this goal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are where we learn our values, build our dreams and create the future we all share.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: When families are strong, our nation is strong.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And when families struggle, we all feel it because we are all connected.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a father of five, I have experienced the joy, the pride and yes, the challenges that come with raising children.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are the foundation of a thriving society and they demand our attention.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, a home is more than four walls and a roof over our heads.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is where we lay down our roots.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a journey of laughter, joy, tears and exhaustion.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I cannot imagine life without my three girls – Ella, Katie and Poppy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They feature a lot in my speeches in this House over the past 10 years because they are a part of almost every aspect of my life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I love seeing the world through their eyes – their pure, untainted view of the world and how they view the world without lens of discrimination.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In a "Singapore Made for Families", I hope more couples can experience this for themselves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Over the years, we have made great progress in our parenthood policies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have our slew of financial assistance, we have increased parental leave and we have made FWAs a reality.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we celebrate what we have done, there is yet more that we can do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, I am continuing to speak up for parents to have more time with their children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first ask is that we increase childcare leave and provide it on a per child basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Yes, I have asked for this many, many times now and I am asking for it again because I know how precious time is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is six days, no matter whether you have one, two, three, four or more children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It does not make sense for two reasons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, we must remember that most childcare centres are closed for about seven-and-a-half days a year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We give parents six days of childcare leave and childcare centres close for about seven-and-a-half days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For couples, who have a combined 12 days of childcare leave, almost more than half is already wiped out from school closures.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What about parents who have children in kindergarten and also in primary schools?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The school closures might not coincide and they face an even more severe shortage of childcare leave and, for them, having childcare leave on a per child basis is very much needed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, our policy seems to suggest that our children will fall sick all at the same time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They fall sick at different times and so, again, how sure are we that six days of childcare leave for all our children is sufficient?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just over the week, a parent shared with me about how his child contracted the dreaded hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On Monday, the child contracted a fever and went to the doctor.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The child was not diagnosed with HFMD and was given a medical certificate (MC) for three days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On Monday night, very night itself, spots started to appear on the child and he suspected it was HFMD.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On Tuesday, he brought her back to the doctor and her HFMD was confirmed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She was given six days of MC until Sunday.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On Sunday, the child was cleared of HFMD, but had an infection due to an insect bite and was given another five days of MC.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I feel tired for the parents just by sharing the above but that is the reality for many, many parents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At one shot, this would have wiped out 10 days of his leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What about leave for the six days of annual school closures?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I should add that this parent has three children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He would not have any leave left if his other two children subsequently contracted HFMD, which does have an incubation period.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He would have no more leave left if any one of his three children fell sick again at any point in the year and we are only in January.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are 11 more months of the year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just over the past week, I also received a letter from my daughter's primary school informing us that there are HFMD cases in school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We were strongly urged to immediately seek medical attention if our children are not feeling well and to allow them to rest at home until the end of their medical leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is common sense and good advice from a public health perspective.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this can also be incredibly difficult for working parents who do not have sufficient leave entitlements.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Without sufficient childcare leave, parents who run out of childcare leave then face a choice between being there for their sick child or go to work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They could, of course, take their annual leave, but many do not have sufficient annual leave too.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can relieve more parents from the stress of this decision by increasing childcare leave and providing it on a per child basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Your six days of childcare leave entitlement is lost when your youngest child enters primary school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: You now get extended childcare leave of only two days, again, if your youngest child is in primary school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But us parents know that a primary school kid cannot look after themselves when they are sick.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What happens when the school is closed for the day or ends early?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just in January, most parents would have used up two days of their extended childcare leave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For those not in Primary 1, school is closed on 2 January.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: School also ended early at 10.30 am on 28 January 2025 for Chinese New Year celebrations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Your extended childcare leave is gone in just the first month of the year.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What about all the other days of primary school closure or early closure?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, on Youth Day, National Day, Teachers' Day, PSLE marking days, Honours Day and Primary 1 Orientation, just to name a few in my own daughter's primary school.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Being a parent is the most rewarding and also the most demanding job.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As every parent knows, every day, you make so many difficult decisions and impossible decisions: choosing between sleep, work, time for yourself and your spouse, chores and your children.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is wishing to rewind time, while begging for more.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But what a beautiful mess it is." In a "Singapore Made for Families", I hope that every parent can be there for their child in moments that will last a lifetime.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, there is still more to be done.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hence, I would like to take this chance to share my ideas with the House.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In my interactions with my residents in Henderson-Dawson, I am very heartened to see that the fathers are very much involved in their fatherhood journey and prioritised spending quality time with their children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope to see clearer and sustained acknowledgment from our Government departments, community organisations and the media of the crucial role that fathers play in the development and the well-being of children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Research has shown that their involvement can lead to better emotional, social, behavioural and cognitive outcomes for children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Highlighting these benefits through public campaigns and community events can help raise awareness about the positive impact of active fatherhood.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   While paternity leave has been extended in recent years, some fathers may still feel the pressure to return to work quickly or fear professional consequences or judgement from others if they take full advantage of the leave.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Employers should offer more flexible options for working fathers, such as part-time work, work-from-home or extended paternity leave, without stigma.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I believe that the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests that was rolled out recently on 1 December 2024 will come in very useful in this regard. : It takes a village to raise a child, especially when both parents are working.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Most families will have in place arrangements for the care of their children while the parents are at work, tapping on grandparents, domestic helpers and childcare centres.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are lucky to have such options, but I also know of childcare centres who have had to impose penalty fees on parents who are late in picking up their children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While we may not be ready to explore the option of night nurseries, like in Sweden, shall we have in place policies to support the staffing needs of childcare centres so that they can accommodate parents who are late?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How about setting industry guidelines for the extension of time as a service option, rather than being imposed as a penalty fee?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For families with older children, including those in primary school and secondary school, they face a different set of challenges and worries, especially when it comes to education-related stress.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: MOE has been taking the initiative to redefine success beyond merely achieving high scores and, instead, tilt towards cultivating skills for lifelong learning and adaptability.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Short-term sacrifices and investments would be necessary to achieve our long-term goal of building stronger Singaporean families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that when families are strong, our society will be strong.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Building on this strong foundation, the Government is committed to supporting all families as they journey through key stages of life, from couples seeking to get married and raise families, to parents with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Marriage aspirations among young Singaporeans remain strong and the Government will continue to work with our partners to support young Singaporeans to build their own future families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling suggested piloting an initiative to allow young couples to hold their wedding in an iconic, historical and beautiful public institution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since 2022, couples have had the option of holding their solemnisation ceremony at the picturesque Family Zone @ Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Registry of Marriages (ROM) and Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) at Canning Rise has also been a cherished venue for couples embarking on their marital journeys for over four decades.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To better meet the needs of couples, the current ROM/ROMM site will be undergoing redevelopment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum suggested providing Marriage Preparation Courses to assist newlyweds in developing skills and mindset for a strong and lasting marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Families for Life (FFL) movement, led by the FFL Council, brings together various partners to offer marriage programmes to provide pre-marital education through the FFL@Community initiative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The goal is to equip soon-to-weds and newlyweds with the necessary family skills to strengthen their marriage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng suggested to enhance training for caregivers and Ms Nadia Samdin mentioned community circles for new parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum proposed establishing a Family Ambassadors Programme to guide and provide resources to families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under FFL@Community, families can conveniently access parenting and grandparenting programmes, as well as parent peer support groups formed and led by volunteers, to equip themselves to step into their roles more confidently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong has highlighted, FFL@Community has been expanded to 18 towns today and we are on target to roll out nationwide to all towns by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government has also launched Grow Well SG recently, a new national health promotion strategy which aims to inculcate healthier lifestyles in children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Miss Rachel Ong and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum mentioned concerns around screen time and social media use among children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under Grow Well SG, ECDA has incorporated explicit guidelines on screen time into the Early Childhood Development Centres Code of Practice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To help educators internalise these guidelines, ECDA will provide guidance on screen use within the upcoming Educators' Guide for the Early Years Development Framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also collaborating with partners to develop accessible resources, so that parent and caregivers can be equipped to reinforce these habits at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Besides strengthening marriage relationships, we have also enhanced our support for parents, especially for those with young children and who need to balance caregiving and work responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested supporting families by providing more places and lowering fees at Government-supported preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, preschools now play a key role in meeting families' caregiving needs and complement parents in supporting our children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have invested significantly in early childhood care and education in recent years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Much of this funding is channelled towards building more infant care and childcare places and improving their affordability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We note Mr Xie Yao Quan's suggestion to increase the basic subsidy, which we provide to all Singaporean children attending preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Basic subsidy is only one of several avenues ensuring preschool affordability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In recent years, the Government has enhanced preschool affordability via other means to effectively lower families' preschool expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children attending Government-supported preschools, infant and childcare fees are capped.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For the past decade, parents have seen their out-of-pocket payment for fees decrease as there is significant funding provided by ECDA to these Government-supported preschools to lower fee caps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For full-day childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool, a middle-income household pays around $200 today, less than half of what they would have paid 10 years ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With the enhancements to the CDA and First Step Grant since February 2023, middle-income households with their child enrolled in Anchor Operator preschools can tap on CDA monies to fully cover four years of childcare expenses if they save up to the co-matching cap.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also significantly increased infant care and childcare capacity and built them in areas where families with young children are concentrated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Hany Soh spoke about the challenges that parents with young children face in securing preschool places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To plan for new preschool places, ECDA analyses the demographics, projected resident birth cohort, enrolment trends and existing supply in each planning area, especially in BTO developments, to meet projected demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To ensure that these preschools are operational when residents move in, ECDA facilitates Anchor Operators' early access to technical plans and arranges site visits so that renovations can commence once the keys are handed over.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The preschool landscape as a whole has changed significantly since ECDA was set up about a decade ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In particular, we set our ambitions high and made a decisive move to expand Government-supported preschool places.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Back in 2019, then-Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong committed at the National Day Rally that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in Government-supported preschools by around 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By the end of this year, 2025, we will achieve our commitment to provide enough Government-supported preschool places to cater to 80% of preschoolers, allowing the vast majority of Singaporean families to benefit from accessible, affordable and quality preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To support the aggressive expansion of preschool capacity, we have also made moves to attract, retain and develop early childhood educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong suggested increasing staff-child ratios in preschools to support the well-being of educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The staff-child ratio requirements are minimum requirements to ensure the safety and well-being of children, though in practice, preschools can and do operate with more staff than required.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA has made concrete moves to improve the career proposition and working conditions of preschool educators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes salary enhancements and the removal of the requirement for childcare centres to operate on Saturdays from this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In October 2024, we also appointed relief staff service providers for the sector to have access to a pool of affordable short-term manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is to allow educators to take time off for their personal or professional needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While still a relatively new initiative, we have been encouraged by the interest and take-up rate thus far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, we are exploring innovative new ways to better cater to the differing caregiving needs of parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In December 2024, ECDA launched a new childminding pilot for infants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under this pilot, parents can engage childminders to look after their infants in the childminders' homes or in a community setting.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With subsidies, parents using these services full-time will pay around $700 a month, lower than the cost of most childminding services today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While the pilot is still in the early stages of ramping up, we are encouraged by the signs of interest from parents thus far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other parents who may prefer more personalised attention and greater flexibility in their infant care arrangements can consider tapping on this option.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As we strengthen our support for families, we recognise that certain groups face unique challenges and we have provided additional upstream support for them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Syed Harun mentioned the need to support single-parent families, such as those who have undergone marital separation, as well as children in these families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For married couples facing relationship challenges, the Strengthening Families Programme @ Family Service Centre (FAM@FSC) provides a continuum of support that begins even before they reach the point of divorce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, through the provision of family counselling and related resources on the Family Assist portal, we hope to help families overcome their differences and remain intact as a unit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Nonetheless, we understand that there will be cases where some familial relationships cannot be repaired.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In such instances, the well-being of the children is a paramount consideration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is why, from July 2024, we had mandated that all divorcing couples with minor children must attend the Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme (CPP), including those who are filing for divorce on the simplified track.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The CPP encourages cooperative co-parenting post-divorce and supports parents to make informed decisions that prioritise the well-being of their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For lower-income families, we have moved in recent years to empower them, over and above continuing our support via ComCare.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong has observed, the preschool participation rate of children aged three to four years from lower-income families is lower than the national average.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have taken steps to close this gap by addressing the practical barriers that these families face.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This means that lower-income families can pay as low as $3 per month for full-day childcare in an Anchor Operator preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we have proactively reached out to lower-income families and incentivised them to enrol their children into preschool in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We expanded the Preschool Outreach Programme to more lower-income families to encourage and facilitate their children's enrolment in preschool by age three.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While still in its early days, we hope that the Package will also contribute to an improvement in preschool enrolment and attendance rates for these families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With the above moves, we hope that lower-income families will have greater assurance that they can secure a preschool place and can afford to send their children to preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked whether it is possible to make student care more affordable for lower-income families, by enhancing and streamlining the Student Care Fee Assistance scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The scheme is designed such that families will co-pay a reasonable amount according to their means, should they require the use of student care centres as a caregiving option after school hours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The median fee at student care centres has been stable at around $295 a month over the past few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will consider the Member's suggestions as we review the Student Care Fee Assistance to ensure that student care prices remain reasonable for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our efforts to support families would not be possible without the contributions of various agencies, stakeholders and volunteers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It takes a collective, whole-of-society effort to make Singapore a place where all families can grow and thrive.
