text: Mr Leong, if you have new clarifications, I will allow it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But there is no need to make the same point again.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Does the Minister agree that when I say we set a target, we are not actually trying to force Singaporeans to have babies.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We are saying that as a policy objective, when we implement policies, we need an objective.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, like when you build infrastructure, there is a population target that you are looking at.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Does the Minister agree that we cannot be just implementing policies without thinking about whether those policies will yield a certain amount of results or not, and what that certain amount of results is, is equivalent to a target, whether it is a soft target or a hard target?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think I have made my point already.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, we can say we want to build X kilometres of roads.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But I think it would be very difficult to say to Singaporeans, "You must produce X number of babies".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I think what Mr Leong should appreciate is that, for infrastructure maybe, for certain things, economic things, you can set certain specific targets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And we hope that Singaporeans will be able to respond to that because the policies that we are putting in place have been based on the feedback that they have given us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can I invite Ms Hany Soh to do your wrap-up?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I would also like to take this opportunity to thank our Ministry staff and Parliamentary Secretariat staff, officers and librarians for all of their support rendered to us.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Given that the Chinese New Year holiday was just last week, all of us would have spent our Chinese New Year break preparing for today's debate amidst our family commitments, attending to your parental and caregiving duties and constituent works.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: As I was performing research and drafting my speeches at home, and during the pockets of time I had during visiting, the moments at which I was momentarily distracted by my two young kids calling out to me, serve as reminders of the impetus for filing today's Motion.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: All of us should experience the greatest joy and bliss that comes from starting and building a family.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: No doubt it will present challenges unique to each family unit as Members would have understood through our engagements with Singaporeans, and this House has heard, in the course of today's debate.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: However, as it is the case that families are the building blocks of society in Singapore, the whole-of-society is here to support all of us in reciprocity.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: By tradition, the seventh day of Chinese New Year is known as 人日, the day on which humans were created, which would make it a rather more apt occasion for us to discuss topics relating to family formation.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Per Ms Nadia Samdin's characterisation, it indeed takes a village to raise a child.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: This village, according to Assoc Prof Razwana Begum's speech earlier, hit the nail on the head of this Motion – the Government, community and private sectors need to come together to adapt, develop and maintain policies and programmes that are contemporary evidence-based and responsive to the diverse needs and circumstances of all families, including those considering starting a family.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: It requires as much as and no less than a whole-of-society's resolve and effort.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: In reviewing and updating policies and programmes, it is important that agencies seek the views and wishes of families and potential families of all descriptions and that these views and wishes are respectfully considered and acted upon where feasible.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I wish to illustrate the notion of this village further, inspired by my Parliamentary colleagues' speeches today.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: In this village, the children include those from single-parent families, blended or step-families, as shared by Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: In the current and future Singapore context, this village must comprise the following infrastructures.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Apart from the hardware, we would also need the heartware to make this village a conducive and enjoyable place to raise our children.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: To make this possible, we would also need the village to be packed with social and physical activities, such as bringing youths together to better understand each other and bond – having heard Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Ng Ling Ling and what I have shared in my opening speech.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: We also need to create all-inclusive opportunities to encourage families comprising the young old, the differently abled to bond, intra-family as described by Miss Rachel Ong, Mr Yip Hon Weng, and even further, inter-family, as shared by Dr Syed Harun.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Our environment ought to also encourage the creation and development of self-help support groups in order to evolve organically.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: We will do well at the family unit level and societal level in sharing personal past experiences of first-timer parents or caregivers overcoming the challenges they encountered.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: On this, I wholeheartedly agree with Ms Nadia Samdin.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: An essential element to this Motion vision is maintaining a strong social compact in the village, in which breadwinners are confident enough to balance the economics and emotions of working and caregiving.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Ms Jean See, Ms Yeo Wan Ling, Mr Faisal Manap accurately described the importance on this.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Of course, as with everything, striking the right balance is critical.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: We cannot neglect understanding employers in the village who encourage their employees to adopt family-friendly practices while sustaining productivity, certainly with the help of the Government.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Louis Chua and Mr Mark Lee rightly reminded us of this.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: We cannot overstate the value of parents being present and hands-on in our children's growing phase.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The importance of the father's role has been a theme that we have been exploring and that the one that should ideally in fact and be seen to be equal to that of a mother's.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: However, each family is unique and so are its circumstances.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Every parent has autonomy to calibrate his or her parenting and caregiving part with support on the ready to be given by the Government.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: I was immensely moved by Mr Zhulkarnain's anecdote on his daughter asking him to help her.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Many of us, including Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Louis Chua and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum, have also underscored the importance of ensuring parents have sufficient time to dedicate to their children.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: This was also endorsed and concurred by Minister of State Gan.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, Ms Nadia Samad and Dr Syed Harun also stand behind this point.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: The union, as highlighted by Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Ms Jean See, also play a crucial role.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Having had myself to step away from work and return twice, I am grateful to those who have spoken, including Mr Desmond Choo and Ms Yeo Wan Ling for looking out for all mothers in this regard.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Much has been said and I have every confidence that even more will be done to support Singaporeans in starting and raising families.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: If I may conclude with a message to my fellow Singaporeans: please trust that this House will be with you along every step of your journey to starting and raising your family.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have now come to the conclusion of the debate which has taken us more than seven hours.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The original Motion is now before the House.
